name: Safe activation and parallel rollout
opener: 🚦 New behaviour heading for real people — deploying it and switching it on are two separate decisions.
explainer: Both versions can live in the same deployed service. The current version can remain the default while selected people test the revision. A switch can return everyone to the current version without reverting or redeploying.

failureModes.prompt: Should the revision replace the current feature in staging, or should both versions run together so only selected people test it first?
failureModes.why: it decides who meets the new behaviour before anyone trusts it

options.label: Parallel rollout
options.consequence: both versions are deployed; selected users test the revision while everyone else stays on the current one

options.label: Direct replacement
options.consequence: simpler to build, but every staging user meets the revision at once

options.label: Separate preview environment
options.consequence: strongest isolation, at the cost of another service to run and maintain

failureModes.provenBy: a test proving the current route still runs the existing implementation when the switch is off
failureModes.fact: Knight Capital lost $440 million in 45 minutes because an old code path woke up on one of eight servers. Which version runs where is the whole question.

failureModes.prompt: Who should be able to turn the revision on for themselves?
failureModes.why: it decides whether a curious stranger can switch on half-finished behaviour

options.label: A named list of signed-in testers
options.consequence: you control exactly who sees it; the list needs maintaining

options.label: Anyone with an internal role
options.consequence: less bookkeeping, and anyone who gains the role gains the feature

options.label: A share of all users
options.consequence: good for measuring, but you cannot choose who is included

failureModes.recommended: A named list of signed-in testers
failureModes.provenBy: a test proving someone outside the list cannot switch the revision on by editing a request
failureModes.fact: If the switch is read from something the phone sends, anyone can send it. Cohorts have to be decided by the server.

failureModes.prompt: With the switch off, should everything work exactly as it does today?
failureModes.why: cleaning up shared code is how today's behaviour changes by accident

options.label: Byte-for-byte the same
options.consequence: safest, and shared cleanup must be proven not to change it

options.label: Close enough is fine
options.consequence: quicker to build, and any slip reaches everyone rather than the testers

failureModes.provenBy: a regression test proving the switch-off response is unchanged from today's
failureModes.fact: The most common parallel-rollout bug is not in the new path. It is a shared helper that both paths now share.

failureModes.prompt: Should the two versions be allowed to share saved results and stored records?
failureModes.why: mixed results are hard to spot and harder to unpick afterwards

options.label: Keep them separate
options.consequence: each version has its own saved copies; slightly more storage

options.label: Let them share
options.consequence: cheaper, and one version can serve the other's answers without anyone noticing

failureModes.provenBy: a test proving neither version can read or overwrite the other's saved entry
failureModes.fact: A shared cache key is how a switched-off user ends up served the new version's answer.

failureModes.prompt: If the revision misbehaves, should you be able to switch it off for everyone without a new release?
failureModes.why: it decides whether a bad afternoon needs a code change and a redeploy

options.label: Yes, a server-side switch
options.consequence: recovery in seconds; the server must always outrank the app

options.label: No, fix and redeploy
options.consequence: one less control to build, and every recovery takes a full release

failureModes.provenBy: a test proving the server's off switch beats every cohort and every app-side choice
failureModes.fact: A rollback you can perform in a meeting is worth more than one that needs a deploy pipeline.

failureModes.prompt: If the app and the server disagree about which version is on, what should happen?
failureModes.why: phones update on their own schedule, so the two sides will disagree eventually

options.label: Fall back to the current version
options.consequence: nobody sees a broken screen; some testers quietly get the old behaviour

options.label: Show a clear message
options.consequence: honest about the mismatch, and interrupts the person

failureModes.recommended: Fall back to the current version
failureModes.provenBy: a test proving an unsupported app-and-server combination degrades without an error screen
failureModes.fact: Old app versions live for months. Every flag that crosses the phone-server line eventually meets one.

failureModes.prompt: Should we record which version actually ran for each request?
failureModes.why: without it, a comparison between the two versions cannot be trusted

options.label: Record version, cohort and outcome
options.consequence: you can compare honestly; slightly more logging cost

options.label: Record errors only
options.consequence: cheaper, and a silent fallback looks like a success

failureModes.provenBy: a test proving the log names the version that actually executed, not the one requested
failureModes.fact: If a request falls back to the old path and the log still says new, every measurement after that is fiction.

failureModes.prompt: Must records written by the revision still be readable by the current version?
failureModes.why: testers and everyone else share one database while both versions run

options.label: Yes, always readable
options.consequence: changes must only add, never reshape; safe to switch off at any moment

options.label: No, the revision owns its own records
options.consequence: cleaner new design, and switching off strands whatever the testers created

failureModes.provenBy: a test proving a record written by the revision is still readable and writable on the current path
failureModes.fact: Turning a feature off is easy. Turning off the data it already wrote is not.
